# Universal Magic Noise Cost

A fixed, globally universal stabilizer factory transforms copies of an
unknown nonstabilizer pure qubit into a fixed CCZ state, exactly at zero noise,
while suppressing independent input depolarization to error order d.
At fixed target success alpha under a nearest-stabilizer infidelity promise
eta >= eta0, the optimal maximum raw-copy cost is Theta_alpha(d/eta0).

Canonical routes:
- README.md: question, main result, source attribution and scope.
- science/model.md: all quantifiers, accepted free maps, noise convention.
- science/results.md: T1 and the proof dependencies.
- science/converse.md: full low-excitation kernel, binomial yield bound,
  six-root multiplicity, and the geometric projection envelope.
- science/construction.md: inherited concentration and correcting-code
  primitives, arbitrary fault pattern handling, all-integer code selection,
  buffering, conditioning and finite-noise bound.
- science/finite_protocols.md: explicit 48-copy quadratic witness, full
  six-qubit noisy input instrument, and output-error conventions.
- science/interpretation.md: physical meaning and boundary.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: primary and internal contribution comparison.
- references/references.bib: structured bibliography.
- verification/README.md: commands, what is verified and what remains analytic.

Do not silently equate:
  pure-input symmetry with the support of an iid noisy tensor input;
  joint two-output error with retained single-output error;
  a geometric projection ceiling with an attainable free operation;
  the necessary n>=6d with a construction at that copy count;
  direction-uniform success under eta>=eta0 with global universality;
  ideal gates with realistic gate/noise overhead;
  the first-order Rizzo-Leone sextic with this noise-forced order-d kernel.

The correcting codes, six-copy inner concentrator, and finite detector
are inherited. The converse and joint order/yield copy law are the
consequential added contribution. The 30-milestone educational map and
source bridge are furnished only after the author selects a single anchor.
